subject: On-prem packaging: operator credits, entry fee swap & SLA exceptions
messages:
From: Kendra Ortiz <kendra.ortiz@medilogic.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai
Cc: Mike Chen <mike.chen@medilogic.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Packaging question — entry fee vs operator credits, SLA needs

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed with the latency profile on short sequences. We're starting procurement conversations internally and a couple of items came up that will determine which path we take (hosted vs on-prem). Can you confirm if Redwood will consider: 

- Swapping a portion of the one-time platform entry fee into usable operator credits (we'd use credits for initial capacity and operator licenses at our sites)
- Temporary premium support credits during the 90-day pilot (we require 24/7 P1 if we bring critical triage on-prem)
- Any quantization/edge-node licensing constraints — Medilogic expects a mix of central GPU pools + local inference nodes that may use 8-bit quantized models

Attached is a short list of questions we compiled (Medilogic_SOW_questions.pdf). Our procurement lead (Mike) is on copy.

Would you and your commercial team be open to a structure that amortizes some entry fee into credits and a short premium support waiver? We're targeting a Q1 pilot start and need a final commercial outline by end of the month.

Cheers,
Kendra Ortiz
Head of ML Ops
Medilogic

Attachments: Medilogic_SOW_questions.pdf
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Kendra Ortiz <kendra.ortiz@medilogic.com>
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Packaging question — entry fee vs operator credits, SLA needs

Hi Kendra — great to hear. Short answer: yes, we can be flexible. Draft thoughts below (high level) so you have something to show procurement: 

1) Entry fee swap: we can convert up to 30% of the platform entry fee into operator credits valid for 12 months. Credits apply to operator licenses and burst capacity within the private deployment construct.

2) Pilot support credits: we can grant 90 days of Premium Support (24/7 P1 coverage) as a credit during the pilot window. After the pilot the customer can choose Standard or Premium at list rates, or we can amortize some of the remaining credits into a longer-term retainer.

3) Quantization/edge nodes: we don't license quantized kernels separately. Edge nodes that run quantized variants are covered by operator licenses; for very large fleet counts we can offer a discounted operator tier (volume-based).

I'm attaching an initial quote (20261215_markus_onprem_quote_v1.pdf) with two packaging options: (A) entry-fee-first-year amortize 30% into credits; (B) smaller amortization + steeper first-year SRE retainer.

If you're comfortable, I'll loop in our procurement lead (Priyom) and legal to check redlines. Happy to hop on a quick call tomorrow if that helps.

Cheers,
Markus Klein
VP, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20261215_markus_onprem_quote_v1.pdf
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Packaging question — entry fee vs operator credits, SLA needs

Priyom / Laura / Aditya / Monica — forwarding Kendra's asks. Quick internal alignment:

- Kendra asked for 30% swap into operator credits + 90 days premium support. I sent a v1 quote.
- Priyom: do we have margin to move to 35% and extend credits to 18 months if it speeds signature?
- Laura: they may ask to cap audit/escrow liability in redlines; we should preempt language around observability/exfil controls for private installs.
- Aditya: any revenue recognition flags with moving entry fee to credits? Finance needs DCF guidance if they want amortization over 12 months vs immediate recognition.

My preference is to offer a slightly more generous commercial (35% swap, credits valid 18 months) but with explicit exit/rollback triggers (if they decommission within 12 months, unused credits expire). Also propose we grant the first month of SRE on-call hours as waived rather than full SOW credit — easier operationally.

Thoughts? I'd like to finalize language before replying to Kendra again.

-Markus
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Kendra Ortiz <kendra.ortiz@medilogic.com>
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 16 Dec 2026 14:47:00 -0800
Subject: Updated commercial offer & next steps

Hi Kendra — thanks for the quick turnaround. We had an internal read with finance and legal and have an updated offer that should map to procurement expectations while keeping contract guardrails simple. Highlights below (summary, see attached quote and SOW redlines):

- Entry fee swap: Redwood will convert 35% of the platform entry fee into operator credits. Credits are redeemable against operator licenses and burst capacity for 18 months from effective date.
- Pilot support: we will provide 90 days of Premium Support as a credited service during the pilot. Additionally, we'll waive the first month of the SRE on-call retainer (if you elect an SRE retainer).
- SLA: we will support a 1-hour P1 response objective under Premium Support. Legal requested a definition clarifier; we've kept the P1 definition conservative and added an operational escalation ladder in the SOW.
- Exit/rollback: unused credits expire at 18 months. If Medilogic exits within 12 months we reserve the right to claw back credits pro-rata (standard rehab clause).

Attachments: 20261216_markus_onprem_quote_v2.pdf, redlines_medilogic_sow_v1.docx

Next steps:
1) If this maps, sign the DocuSign we'll send (I'll ask Priyom to generate the envelope with the quote & SOW).
2) Laura will review any redlines you return — we can usually resolve 1-2 minor redline items in parallel with signature.

DocuSign link will be provided in the next email. Are you available for a 30-min call Friday morning if procurement has follow-ups?

Best,
Markus Klein
VP, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20261216_markus_onprem_quote_v2.pdf, redlines_medilogic_sow_v1.docx
From: Kendra Ortiz <kendra.ortiz@medilogic.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mike Chen <mike.chen@medilogic.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Dec 2026 10:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Updated commercial offer & next steps

Markus — thanks, this is helpful and closer to what procurement expected. Two small asks from our legal and procurement teams before we sign: 

1) SLA definition: can we change the P1 impact language to explicitly include production inference outages that affect >50% of requests (current wording references "critical service degradation" which is subjective).
2) Operator credits: can you confirm credits are tied to Medilogic account (non-transferable) but redeemable across sites under the same contract ID? Procurement also asked that unused credits be visible in a billing portal export.

I've attached our redlines (Medilogic_redlines.docx). If you can accept the two bullets above we're close to sending back for signature. We can do the Friday call if you'd like to run procurement through the slight changes.

—Kendra

Attachments: Medilogic_redlines.docx

Subject: Re: On-prem packaging: operator credits, entry fee swap & SLA exceptions — routing for signature

All — we're good to accept Kendra's two asks: Laura will update the P1 wording to the ">50% of requests outage" clause and confirm non-transferability + account-scoped credits visible in portal exports. I'll generate the DocuSign envelope (quote v2 + SOW redlines) and route to Kendra + Mike. Aditya, finance OKs 35% swap amortized as credits for 18 months from a revenue recognition perspective (we'll book the entry fee and contra it with deferred credit liability).

Markus — will send the envelope and copy you when live. Thanks team.

—Priyom Das
